# AI Usage Policy

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This project does **not** accept pull requests that are fully or predominantly AI-generated. AI tools may be utilized solely in an assistive capacity.
>
> Repeated violations of this policy may result in your account being permanently banned from contributing to the project.

Code that is initially generated by AI and subsequently edited will still be considered AI-generated. AI assistance is permissible only when the majority of the configuration is authored by a human contributor, with AI employed exclusively for corrections or to expand on verbose modifications that the contributor has already conceptualized (e.g., generating repeated lines with minor variations).

If AI is used to generate any portion of a change, contributors must adhere to the following requirements:

1. Explicitly disclose the manner in which AI was employed.
2. Perform a comprehensive manual review prior to submitting the pull request.
3. Be prepared to explain every line they submitted when asked about it by a reviewer.
4. It is strictly prohibited to use AI to write your posts for you (bug reports, feature requests, pull request descriptions, GitHub discussions, responding to humans, ...).

# Pull requests

Before submitting your PR:

- Search for existing PRs and issues to prevent duplicating efforts.
- Let the pre-commit hooks run, or invoke `mise run format:check .` and `mise run validate <paths>` manually, and make sure both pass.
- Create separate PRs for each preset or fix, and avoid combining unrelated changes.
- For intricate changes (new datasource, broad regex managers, anything that touches `default.json5`), consider opening an issue first to align expectations.
- Use [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/).
- If your PR becomes stale, rebase it on top of latest `main`.

# Preset guidelines

Each preset should:

- Solve a single, named upstream quirk — one package, one manager, or one datasource per file.
- Use narrow `matchPackageNames` / file patterns so it's inert for consumers who don't use the targeted dependency.
- Carry a `description` on every `packageRule` and `customManager`.
- Avoid bundling unrelated rules. If a quirk has a different audience, split it into a new file.
- Prefer broad `managerFilePatterns` only when the `matchStrings` regex is specific enough to avoid false matches; otherwise scope by path.

When you add a new preset:

1. Place it under the right category subdirectory (`managers/`, `overrides/`, or `versioning/`). Create a new subdirectory if none fit.
2. Add it to the `extends` array in [`default.json`](./default.json).
3. Document caveats (hardcoded values, layout assumptions, etc.) as comments in the preset file itself, near the rule they apply to. The README should not list individual presets — the directory structure is the index.

The `validate` step in [`.github/workflows/validate.yaml`](./workflows/validate.yaml) globs each category directory, so new files are picked up automatically as long as they sit under one.

# Naming guidelines

- Preset filenames are `kebab-case.json5` and match the upstream project name (`llama-cpp.json5`, `talos-factory.json5`).
- The preset's `extends` slug is the filename without the extension (`github>home-operations/renovate-presets:llama-cpp`).
- One preset per upstream project; do not group multiple unrelated projects under a generic name like `overrides.json5`.

# Development

Tooling is managed by [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev). The repo uses [lefthook](https://lefthook.dev) for pre-commit hooks and [GitHub Actions](./workflows/validate.yaml) for CI.

```sh
# Install all tools pinned in .mise.toml (node, lefthook, prettier, renovate).
# A postinstall hook also runs `lefthook install` to wire up the git hooks.
mise install

# Format files (pass paths, or `.` for everything)
mise run format .

# Check formatting (CI runs this against `.`)
mise run format:check .

# Validate presets against Renovate's schema (CI passes the category globs)
mise run validate default.json managers/*.json5 overrides/*.json5 versioning/*.json5 .github/renovate.json5
```

Pre-commit hooks invoke the same `format:check` and `validate` tasks, passing only the staged files. CI re-runs both across the whole repo via [`jdx/mise-action`](https://github.com/jdx/mise-action).

# Documentation

- Documentation is a community effort. When you read Renovate's source or docs to figure out a quirk, add a short summary to the preset's `description` or to README's "Preset notes" so the next person doesn't have to.
- When you notice incorrect or outdated information, please update it.
